subject: Besag model - sum of structured and ustructured spatial effects and their probability.

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Besag model - sum of structured and ustructured spatial effects and their probability.
parts:
Dear group,

I'm working with simple spatial binomial model in the form

f_1 = binary_outcome ~ f(region.struct,
                 model = "besag",
                 graph = "graph.adj",
                 adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE) +
  f(region.un, model="iid") +
  covariate1 + covariate2

m_1 <- inla(f_1, family="binomial", data=data,
            control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

I have two problems.

1) I'd like to get the sum of of exponentiated structured and unstructured effect of

exp(m_1$summary.random$region.struct$"0.5quant")

and

exp(m_1$summary.random$region.struct$"0.5quant")

How can that be achieved? Is this done with lincomb function?

2) As next step, I'd like to get the posterior probabilities of those values for each of the spatial units (so that I can create the map). From where in the model can I obtain them?

Thanks for help!

On 5 Apr 2014, at 18:25, Radoslaw Panczak <r.pa...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear group,

I'm working with simple spatial binomial model in the form

f_1 = binary_outcome ~ f(region.struct,
                 model = "besag",
                 graph = "graph.adj",
                 adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE) +
  f(region.un, model="iid") +
  covariate1 + covariate2

m_1 <- inla(f_1, family="binomial", data=data,
            control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo=TRUE))

I have two problems.

1) I'd like to get the sum of of exponentiated structured and unstructured effect of

exp(m_1$summary.random$region.struct$"0.5quant")

and

exp(m_1$summary.random$region.struct$"0.5quant")

How can that be achieved? Is this done with lincomb function?

Why do you want this?  I don't see any obvious connection to how the model is structured that would motivate looking at the sum of the exponentiated effects.  The model connects the sum of the effects themselves to the binomial probability via a logit-transformation.
Lincomb can give you the distribution for the sum of the effects, but not the sum of non-linearly transformed effects.

Finn

2) As next step, I'd like to get the posterior probabilities of those values for each of the spatial units (so that I can create the map). From where in the model can I obtain them?

Thanks for help!

Finn, Havard,

Thank you for comments. I'm back on the problem (sorry for late replies, it's only a side project where I can work when time is available..).

Quick question:

Would switching from 'besag' model to 'bym' be of help here?

And then reusing the code from Blangiardo et al (2012):

#We now prepare the BYM model and run INLA
library(INLA)
formula <- y ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph=LDN.adj)
mod <- inla(formula,family="poisson",data=data,E=E)

#We calculate zeta=exp(csi) where csi=upsilon + nu
m <- mod$marginals.random$ID[1:Nareas]
zeta <- lapply(m,function(x)inla.emarginal(exp,x))

Thanks again for help.

> Would switching from 'besag' model to 'bym' be of help here?

should not be. the bym-model is just a shorthand for

f(i,model="besag") + f(ii,model="iid")

with a reparametersiation as well, so you get easier access to their
sum.
